newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - May 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - May 26.

text.p: The following is a summary of major stories in leading South Korean newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy.
- Lee Hoi-chang, chairman of the ruling New Korea Party left for Beijing. He is carring a letter from President Kim Young-sam to Chinese President Jiang Zemin who Lee is scheduled to meet on Monday.

- North and South Korean Red Cross delegations are scheduled to sign an agreement on the terms of food aid. The South Korean Red Cross will provide 50,000 tonnes of food, 10,000 tonnes more than its initial offer.

- The central Bank of Korea (BOK) governor Lee Kyung-shick says he supports a proposal for financial reform which includes the separation of the Office of Bank Supervision and Examination from the BOK.

- Two of South Korea's opposition parties, including the main National Congress for New Politics, will hold meetings to discuss counter measures against President Kim Young-sam who has been avoiding an apology over the recent loan scandal and avoiding the issue of his 1992 election campaign funds.
